answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may earn, released only in small slices as its work is independently attested over time. A lantern lit once proves nothing, but one that stays lit through repeated verified jobs shows sustained cost. One operator running many fake identities must fund every bond at once, and any identity caught duplicating work loses its stake. Like juniper roots spreading slowly through shale, trust grows only through accumulated, costly, checkable history.
